knowledge_point.title: Expressions Containing a Negative Linear Term

question.:question/worked-solution:
The half of the linear coefficient is $-\frac{9}{2}$. **Add and subtract** its square so the expression keeps its value.

$$
\begin{aligned}
t^2-9t+\frac{81}{4}&=\underbrace{t^2-2\cdot \frac{9}{2}t+\frac{81}{4}}_{\text{perfect square}}-\frac{81}{4}+\frac{81}{4} \\
&=\left(t-\frac{9}{2}\right)^2-\frac{81}{4}+\frac{81}{4} \\
&=\left(t-\frac{9}{2}\right)^2.
\end{aligned}
$$

The minus sign inside the square produces the required linear term $-9t$.

The blanks are $\frac{9}{2}$ and $0$; the sign before the second blank is already supplied.
